entry_state: AppendixA introduces specified portable exchanges under the common envelope. Corporate, joined-company and real-source packages bind inputs, schemas, references and before/after worlds while retaining finite documentary scope. The operation registry begins with source preparation and review proposals; neither admits a financial claim. Review commitment and the remaining operations follow.
exit_state: The portable registry now covers review, time selection, compilation, history operations, uncertainty evaluation/admission/selection, scenario projection, accounting assessment/authorization/proposal/commit, reporting, explanation, resume and storage exchanges. The common envelope owns expected-head information. Closed accounting-record definitions begin next and remain unfinished.
findings: The short entries are legible and appropriately use the previously explained body semantics as prerequisites for a lookup reference.
History witnesses remain examples, unsupported query expressions remain explicit, and refinements record replacement rather than assuming every correction is intersection.
Uncertainty evaluation never selects its result automatically; admission retains author-stipulated labels; selection does not recompute probability.
Accounting assessment, posting permission, candidate construction and atomic publication have different effects. Expected heads refer to the common envelope as stated at the appendix opening.
Reporting cannot add balancing plugs, explanation cannot substitute today's view, resume cannot hide a model change and import cannot grant financial admission.
